theory.intro: A cumulative frequency histogram shows the running total of scores up to and including each value. Quartiles can be read straight from it, without listing every data value.
facts: Each column's height is the **cumulative frequency** up to and including that score, so the last column's height is the total, $n$.
$Q_1$ sits at position $0.25n$, $Q_2$ (the median) at $0.5n$, and $Q_3$ at $0.75n$.
The minimum is the score of the first column; the maximum is the score of the last column, where the cumulative frequency reaches $n$.
steps: Read the total frequency, $n$, from the height of the last column
Read the score at each position from the histogram, and state the minimum and maximum

mastery.question_text:
A cumulative frequency histogram shows the delivery times (minutes) of courier parcels: $9$ minutes (frequency $4$), $10$ minutes (frequency $k$), $11$ minutes (frequency $5$), $12$ minutes (frequency $3$).
There are $20$ parcels in total.
Find $Q_2$, the median delivery time.

mastery.solution_text:
$Q_3 \text{ position} = 0.75 \times 20 = 15$
$Q_3 = 21$ minutes, with cumulative frequency $18$
$\text{Deliveries longer than } Q_3 = 20 - 18$
$= 2$
